name: Script Module
description: Adds a Script Module (core since WP 6.5): a native ES module WordPress loads with type="module" and lists in its import map, so it can import '@wordpress/interactivity' and other registered modules by bare specifier without a bundler. Generates the module source plus a Registrable that registers it from the build output with dependencies and a version read from the build's .asset.php, and no-ops on WP < 6.5.

inputs.description: PSR-4 namespace for the registration class. Default 'Inc\Services' matches the rtCamp skeleton.

Directory for the registration class. Default 'includes/Services'. The class derives the plugin root by walking two levels up from itself, so keep it two levels deep or adjust the dirname() depth it documents.
PSR-4 namespace for the test class. Default 'Inc\Tests\Services'.
Directory for the test file. Default 'tests/Services'.
Logical module name, e.g. 'lightbox'. Normalised to a PascalCase class name and a kebab-case module slug.
PascalCase class name, derived from name.
Slug half of the module id and the JS filename, derived from name.
Source directory for the module (the input to @wordpress/scripts). Default 'src/js/modules', which the rtCamp skeleton's webpack config already discovers automatically.

Compiled-output directory holding the built module and its generated .asset.php. Default 'build/js/modules'. Override to the project's real build path (the rtCamp skeleton uses 'assets/build/js/modules').
Hook the module is enqueued on: 'wp_enqueue_scripts' for front-end requests, 'enqueue_block_assets' to cover the editor as well.
Vendor half of the module id, conventionally the project text domain, producing '@my-plugin/lightbox'. The engine cannot read a plugin header, so pass it explicitly when it is not 'my-plugin'.

wiring.description: Add the class to a Services module so the framework Loader instantiates it and calls register_hooks(). If no suitable module exists, scaffold one first via `wp-tooling add wp/module --name=Services --kind=registrable`.
